result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A names the decision the research feeds (roadmap plus partner and legal effort), says in advance what result would change the plan, and gives a dated day-by-day schedule with a clear section on what the user must do themselves. Answer B is also strong: it adds useful feasibility questions on regulation, economics and overlap with any existing guarantee. However, it ties less clearly to a specific decision, stretches the designer to about 6 hours in week 2 when they have about 3 a week, and says less plainly which steps a human has to do. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B states the decision the research feeds (whether to put the add-on on the roadmap and spend partner and legal effort on it) and says what result would change the plan. It also separates what the data can answer from what only calls can, and lists plainly what the user must do themselves. A is solid and practical, with good data mining, interviews and a fake door, but it never names the decision as clearly, has no explicit section on human-owned steps, and doesn't flag that showing an insurance price may need legal review before the fake-door test runs.
